name: Question 8
problem:
Solve the initial value problem

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}]x(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The matrix has the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=4\text{i}$ with the corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$*
worked_solution:
We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 8 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}].$ 

We are given the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=4\text{i}$ and the corresponding eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

**Note:** The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}={\overset{―}{\lambda }}_{1}$ is 
${v}_{2}={\overset{―}{v}}_{1}.$ But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=4\text{i}$ and its associated eigenvector is

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{4\text{i}t}.
$$

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{4\text{i}t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1-\text{i} \\ 1\end{aligned}]\cdot (\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\text{i}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t))+\text{i}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\text{i}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}]+\text{i}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}] \\  & ={\text{w}}_{1}(t)+\text{i}{\text{w}}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

The vectors ${w}_{1}$ and ${w}_{2}$ are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & ={c}_{1}{\text{w}}_{1}(t)+{c}_{2}{\text{w}}_{2}(t) \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$ using the initial condition $x(0)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Substituting $t=0$ into the general solution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(0) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}-{c}_{2} \\ {c}_{1}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1} \\ {c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{x}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t) \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡(4t)+\operatorname{sin}⁡(4t)\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

Solve the initial value problem x′(t)=[−48−44]x(t),x(0)=[01].

Hint: The matrix has the eigenvalue λ1=4i with the corresponding eigenvector v1=[1−i1].

a
x(t)=[−2sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]
b
x(t)=[4sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]
c
x(t)=[−sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)−2sin⁡(4t)]
d
x(t)=[sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]
e
x(t)=[2sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

We need to find the eigenvalues and associated eigenvectors of the matrix A=[−48−44].

We are given the eigenvalue λ1=4i and the corresponding eigenvector v1=[1−i1].

Note: The eigenvector corresponding to the second eigenvalue λ2=λ―1 is v2=v―1. But we do not require this eigenvector for solving our system.

The solution that we obtain for the eigenvalue λ1=4i and its associated eigenvector is x1(t)=[1−i1]e4it.

We now express this as a real function. Using Euler's formula, we obtain x1(t)=[1−i1]e4it=[1−i1]⋅(cos⁡(4t)+isin⁡(4t))=[cos⁡(4t)+isin⁡(4t)−icos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)+isin⁡(4t)]=[(cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t))+i(sin⁡(4t)−cos⁡(4t))cos⁡(4t)+isin⁡(4t)]=[cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]+i[sin⁡(4t)−cos⁡(4t)sin⁡(4t)]=w1(t)+iw2(t).

The vectors w1 and w2 are linearly independent. Therefore, the general solution of the system is x(t)=c1w1(t)+c2w2(t)=c1[cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]+c2[sin⁡(4t)−cos⁡(4t)sin⁡(4t)].

Now, we need to find the values of c1 and c2 using the initial condition x(0)=[01]. Substituting t=0 into the general solution gives x(0)=c1[11]+c2[−10][01]=[c1−c2c1][c1c2]=[11].

Finally, the solution to our initial value problem is given by x(t)=[cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)]+[sin⁡(4t)−cos⁡(4t)sin⁡(4t)]=[2sin⁡(4t)cos⁡(4t)+sin⁡(4t)].
